rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the rank-difference does isolate a depreciation-to-price wedge that is plausibly orthogonal to HML, though the reviewer should be aware the surviving content is close to a capital-intensity/dp-to-price tilt that CMA may partially absorb.

Differencing GP/P against AT/P mechanically nets out the price scaling and leaves something very close to gross-profits-to-assets, i.e. a rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability that RMW largely spans, contradicting the claim that FF5 leaves it unpriced.

Self-described as a "near-controlled contrast" with the archived gated-value signal, it reuses the identical yield×indicator template with a level-to-change tweak on the gate — a cosmetic variant unlikely to flip an alpha that was negative for portfolio-composition reasons, and its gate overlaps heavily with the accrual gate proposed alongside it.

Substituting a time-series (own-history) valuation rank for cross-sectional cheapness is a genuinely different design that plausibly escapes HML spanning, and the margin gate is coherently specified — though the margin-trend leg echoes the archived industry sales-yield signal and the TS_RANK window units should be verified.
